title: POC weekly sync - app integration (SDK + tool/function calls + structured output)
meeting_header: Date: 2026-02-24 | Time: 10:00 PST | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Jordan Price, Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Priya Patel, Sofia Martinez
summary: Weekly POC sync to review SDK integration tests, tool/function calling flow, structured output schema results, and next steps for production pilot. SE ran end-to-end tests; found schema validation failures on edge cases and an unexpected latency spike when external tool calls chained. Action items assigned for logs, sample prompts, and security review scheduling.

Jordan to send pricing summary + Dedicated capacity options (due 2026-02-25)
Priya to provide sample prompt set and edge-case examples (due 2026-02-27)
Schedule security review with Arcadia infra (target 2026-03-03)
action_items: Maya Chen: collect SDK logs and structured output validation failures; include full request/response (due 2026-02-26)
Jordan Price: send pricing, Dedicated SLA notes, and link to benchmark spreadsheet (due 2026-02-25)
Priya Patel: upload sample dataset + prompt list to shared drive (due 2026-02-27)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, um let's kick off — 48 minute sync. Maya and I from Redwood; Arcadia team on the line. quick check in, Maya do you wanna start with the e2e run?
[00:22] Maya: yeah sure, I ran the SDK integration tests last night, v0.9.2 of the JS SDK. overall the function-call flow looks good, we validated tool calls to fetch_customer_profile and call_pricing_api. most responses matched the structured schema but we saw about 4% schema validation failures on optional fields.
[00:48] Priya: can you clarify "optional fields"? those are the nested billing items?
[00:54] Maya: yeah it's mainly the line_items array — sometimes the model returned a string instead of an object when the prompt was short, so our JSON schema validator (ajv) flagged it. looks like a prompt engineering edge-case.
[01:11] Liam: is that a Redwood thing or the model variant? curious if quantization/llama variant causing it.
[01:18] Maya: good q. we repro'd it on both hosted and a dedicated small instance; seems model behavior when instructions are ambiguous. we added a stricter function signature in the SDK function_call mode and that reduced failures to ~0.7%.
[01:36] Sofia: timeline — are we still on track for pilot next month?
[01:40] Jordan: yes timeline unchanged but we want to stabilize schema before pilot. hence the ask for Priya's edge-case prompts.
[01:47] Priya: OK I'll upload a set of 120 prompts that hit those flows.
[01:52] Maya: great, that will help. also note we saw a latency spike when tool calls were chained — e.g., call A -> call B -> model call back. chaining external API calls added ~350ms per chain step on average.
[02:06] Liam: is that network overhead or SDK sync behavior?
[02:10] Maya: a bit of both. our SDK currently does sequential tool invocation by default; you can enable parallel tool calls or configure streaming with early partial responses. we demoed parallelization in the test and reduced end-to-end 95p by 220ms.
[02:26] Jordan: quick aside — pricing note: parallel tool calls increase compute but reduce latency; we can show cost delta in the spreadsheet. I'll share the benchmark link after the call.
[02:38] Priya: do you have a recommended pattern for deterministic structured output? we need exact keys for downstream parsing.
[02:44] Maya: yes — use the SDK's function schema + required fields in the JSON schema. also use the structured_output option in the client which forces model to return the specified keys; it helps but still rely on post-validate and a small wrapper to coerce types.
[03:03] Sofia: any notes on KV cache or prefix caching for repeated prompts?
[03:07] Maya: yes, Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching so repeated context is cheap. for this app, cache hits reduced token generation time by about 12% in our tests. but cache requires stable prompt prefixes and watch out for prompt rewriting.
[03:23] Jordan: security question from procurement — Arcadia asked about KMS and audit logs again, can you give the status?
[03:29] Maya: we support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments and HSM options for on-prem. audit logs are available via the Console with token-level traces. for hosted we have SOC 2 + ISO references, I'll attach the compliance pack.
[03:46] Liam: perfect — please add sample logs so our security team can validate.
[03:50] Maya: will do.
[03:52] Priya: on the SDK side, we had one flaky test where streaming stopped mid-response, labeled as timeouts. any idea?
[03:59] Maya: saw that — it was the keepalive setting in our test harness. bumping socket timeout to 90s fixed it in our environment. also recommend using the SDK retry policy for idempotent tool calls.
[04:14] Jordan: regarding Dedicated vs Hosted — what was the latency difference on your benchmark?
[04:19] Maya: hosted 95p was 420ms for our typical payload; Dedicated (g4dn-like profile) 95p was 290ms. with batching tuned for their qps we can hit ~250ms 95p. quantized model variants increase throughput but sometimes add 10-30ms depending on kernel.
[04:40] Liam: do you have an autoscaling config recommendation? our load is spiky — mornings and end of day.
[04:46] Maya: yes, for spiky workloads we suggest a base dedicated pool sized for steady QPS and burst capacity for peaks; we can configure horizontal scale with cooldowns and warm pools to avoid cold-start latency. I'll share a sample autoscale policy.
[05:00] Priya: about the structured output failures — can Maya paste one of the failing responses?
[05:05] Maya: sure, readout: "line_items: "$15 subscription"" instead of {"price":15,"desc":"subscription"}. That was from a 5-token prompt where model truncated. adding explicit examples in the prompt and enforcing the function schema fixed majority.
[05:27] Sofia: any suggestion for fallback if schema fails in prod? we can't crash downstream.
[05:31] Maya: best practice — wrap sanitizer: if JSON parse fails, call a low-cost rerun with more explicit instruction or fallback to a simpler parser. Redwood runtime supports automatic fallback to a compatible model variant; you can also route failures to a batch job for offline correction.
[05:50] Jordan: record action — implement sanitizer + rerun path for schema failures.
[05:55] Priya: about telemetry — what logs should we collect for triage?
[05:59] Maya: include request id, model name + version, function signature used, raw model output, and timing for each tool call. that gives us enough to map failures.
[06:12] Liam: great, we'll plug that into our observability stack.
[06:15] Maya: small note, we saw one environment issue when running the node SDK in a lambda with 512MB memory — tokenization OOM on large batches. recommended memory footprint is 1GB for typical workloads; for heavy batching go higher.
[06:32] Priya: good to know, we're on 1GB for prod so should be fine.
[06:36] Sofia: did you test the function-calling contract with our downstream microservice?
[06:40] Maya: yes, we hit their staging endpoint; found a couple of header mismatches and auth token TTL problems. resolved by adjusting SDK to include bearer token refresh hooks.
[06:50] Priya: can Redwood host the call to our microservice in the Private deployment? we prefer not to egress to public internet.
[06:58] Maya: in Private (VPC) deployment your calls remain in the VPC; no egress required if the microservice sits inside the same network. we'll hand off the network config doc.
[07:08] Jordan: quick question on cost modelling — Priya, what's your 95p qps target?
[07:12] Priya: around 12 qps peak, average 3 qps.
[07:16] Maya: with that profile, a small dedicated pool sized for 12 qps with moderate batching should be cost efficient; I'll run cost sim and include in pricing sheet.
[07:25] Jordan: thanks. Sofia, any product concerns?
[07:28] Sofia: only that we need determinism for downstream analytics. Is there an option to pin model versions per route?
[07:33] Maya: yes you can pin model versions and we support rollouts/canary. also automatic fallback to earlier version if regression detected.
[07:42] Priya: latency when using prefix cache — does that change behavior for structured outputs?
[07:46] Maya: cache just reduces token generation time; structured output behavior depends only on prompt and function schema. one caveat: if prefix caching causes the model to see an older context that changes interpretation, you'll need to ensure your prefix is canonical.
[08:01] Liam: procurement asked about data residency — logs stored where?
[08:04] Maya: for hosted logs are in region and we can configure retention; for Private you're in control. will provide the data residency doc.
[08:12] Jordan: ok let's move to concrete blockers — anything blocking pilot next week?
[08:16] Priya: schema edge-cases and auth for microservice. both resolvable; I'll prioritize prompts and auth token TTL.
[08:25] Maya: also we'll need the sample dataset to complete regression tests.
[08:29] Jordan: recap next steps — Jordan share pricing + benchmark link; Maya share compliance pack and sample autoscale policy; Priya upload prompts and dataset; schedule security review.
[08:42] Sofia: can we try one final full-run with streaming enabled to measure end-to-end latency?
[08:47] Maya: yes we can run a streaming e2e; I'll do that evening and post results.
[08:52] Jordan: great. last Q — any blockers on SDK version pinning?
[08:56] Maya: use v0.9.2 for now; we'll release patch v0.9.3 with the stricter function signature by Friday.
[09:04] Priya: noted. thanks everyone.
[09:07] Jordan: thanks all; we'll follow up in writing. shared artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet (https://redwood.app/benchmarks/arcadia-q1), compliance pack (link sent after), autoscale sample policy (drive link). end.
